result.topic_en: The page gives examples of numbers of the forms 4r+1 and 4ϱ+1 classified relative to a=14, 15, 8, 12, and a fragment (Krafft) claiming that for a prime 4n+1 all divisors of the quadratic residues n−qq−q are also residues; it then begins an observation (N. Fuss) on when xx+1 is divisible by 5², 13² and 17².
result.transcription:
184 L. EULERI OPERA POSTHUMA. Arithmetica.
Exemplum 3. Si $a=2.7=14$ et $4a=56$
$4r+1=1,\ 5,\ 9,\ 13,\ 25,\ 45,\ |\ 57,\ 61,\ 65,\ 69,\ 81,\ 101$
$4\varrho+1=17,\ 29,\ 33,\ 37,\ 41,\ 53,\ |\ 73,\ 85,\ 89,\ 93,\ 97,\ 109$
Exemplum 4. Sit $a=3.5=15$ et $4a=60$
$4r+1=1,\ 17,\ 49,\ 53,\ |\ 61,\ 77,\ 109$
$4\varrho+1=13,\ 29,\ 37,\ 41,\ |\ 73,\ 89,\ 97$
Corollarium. Si fuerit $a=ffg$, quia factor $ff$ in ordine $r$ continet numeros, in ordine $\varrho$ autem nullos, termini communes ordinibus $r$ sunt omnes, qui pro $g$ habentur, at termini ordinibus $\varrho$ communes sunt nulli, ergo pro hoc casu ordo $4r+1$ congruit cum numero $g$, similique modo congruit ordo $4\varrho+1$. Id quod his casibus apparet
$a=8,\ 4a=32\begin{cases}4r+1=1,\ 9,\ 17,\ 25,\ |\ 33,\ 41,\ 49,\ 57,\ |\ 65,\ 73,\ 81,\ 89\\ 4\varrho+1=5,\ 13,\ 21,\ 29,\ |\ 37,\ 45,\ 53,\ 61,\ |\ 69,\ 77,\ 85,\ 93\end{cases}$
$a=4.3=12,\ 4a=48\begin{cases}4r+1=1,\ 13,\ 25,\ 37,\ |\ 49,\ 61,\ 73,\ 85,\ |\ 97\\ 4\varrho+1=5,\ 17,\ 29,\ 41,\ |\ 53,\ 65,\ 77,\ 89,\ |\end{cases}$
A. m. T. I. p. 226—235.
22.
(Krafft.)
Si fuerit $4n+1$ numerus primus, in residuis quadratorum non solum hi numeri $n-qq-q$, sed etiam omnes eorum divisores occurrent.
Quia numerus residuorum diversorum est $=2n$, omnia prodibunt, si loco $q$ substituantur numeri
$0,\ 1,\ 2,\ 3\ \ldots\ (2n-1)$,
ergo haec residua erunt, ut sequens tabella indicat, ubi ultima columna ostendit ea quadrata, unde haec residua nascuntur:
$n-0 \qquad 4n^2$
$n-2 \qquad (2n-1)^2$
$n-6 \qquad (2n-2)^2$
$n-12 \qquad (2n-3)^2$
$n-20 \qquad (2n-4)^2$
$\vdots \qquad \vdots$
$-4n^2+3n \qquad 1$
Nunc autem demonstrandum restat, etiam omnes factores horum residuorum esse residua, quod eo magis est mirandum, quod cum etiam hae formulae
$\lambda(4n+1)+n-qq-q$
pariter residua exhibeant, tamen non omnes factores etiam futuri sint residua.
A. m. T. I. p. 255.
23.
(N. Fuss I.)
Observatio. Formula $xx+1$ divisibilis erit per sequentes numeros quadratos:
I. per $5^2$ si fuerit $x=5^2t\pm 7$
II. » $13^2$ » $x=13^2t\pm 70$
III. » $17^2$ » $x=17^2t\pm 38$

items.quote: Si fuerit $4n+1$ numerus primus, in residuis quadratorum non solum hi numeri $n-qq-q$, sed etiam omnes eorum divisores occurrent.
items.english: If 4n+1 is a prime number, then among the residues of squares occur not only these numbers n−qq−q but also all their divisors.

items.quote:
Nunc autem demonstrandum restat, etiam omnes factores horum residuorum esse residua, quod eo magis est mirandum, quod cum etiam hae formulae
$\lambda(4n+1)+n-qq-q$
pariter residua exhibeant, tamen non omnes factores etiam futuri sint residua.
items.english: Now it remains to be proved that all factors of these residues are also residues, which is all the more remarkable because, although the formulae λ(4n+1)+n−qq−q likewise give residues, not all their factors will also be residues.
